t: Make K-Subarray Sums Equal — GCD Cycles and Median
o: All circular subarrays of length k must have equal sums. Comparing adjacent windows: sum starting at i equals sum starting at i+1 iff arr[i] == arr[(i+k) mod n]. So equality for all windows forces arr[i] == arr[i+k] for every i, partitioning indices into g = gcd(n, k) independent cycles. Within each cycle all values must become equal; with unit increment/decrement cost, the cheapest common target is the median of the cycle's values. Example: arr=[1,4,1,3], k=2, g=2: cycles {0,2}->{1,1} cost 0, {1,3}->{4,3} cost 1, total 1.
k: Equal adjacent window sums imply arr[i] == arr[i+k] for all i (mod n).
Indices split into gcd(n,k) cycles under steps of k; each cycle must be flattened to one value.
Unit-cost flattening is minimized at the median, giving sum |a - median|.

a.i: Extract each of the g cycles (indices i, i+k, i+2k, ... mod n), sort it, and add the absolute deviations from its median. Sorting each cycle costs O(L log L) with total L = n.
s: For each start in [0, g): collect the cycle values, sort, take median, add sum of |v - median|.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def makeSubKSumEqual(self, arr: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        from math import gcd
        n = len(arr)
        g = gcd(n, k)
        ans = 0
        for s in range(g):
            cyc = []
            j = s
            while True:
                cyc.append(arr[j])
                j = (j + k) % n
                if j == s: break
            cyc.sort()
            m = cyc[len(cyc) // 2]
            ans += sum(abs(v - m) for v in cyc)
        return ans

a.t: O(n log n) — each element belongs to exactly one cycle; sorting dominates.

a.i: Replace sorting with nth_element/quickselect to find the median in expected O(L) per cycle, yielding O(n) expected total — worthwhile for very large inputs.
s: Use nth_element (or statistics-of-list selection) to get the median without full sorting.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def makeSubKSumEqual(self, arr: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        import random
        from math import gcd
        def median(lst):
            lst = lst[:]
            random.shuffle(lst)
            tgt = len(lst) // 2
            lo, hi = 0, len(lst) - 1
            while True:
                p = lst[lo]; i, j = lo, hi
                while i <= j:
                    while lst[i] < p: i += 1
                    while lst[j] > p: j -= 1
                    if i <= j: lst[i], lst[j] = lst[j], lst[i]; i += 1; j -= 1
                if tgt <= j: hi = j
                elif tgt >= i: lo = i
                else: return lst[tgt]
        n = len(arr); g = gcd(n, k); ans = 0
        for s in range(g):
            cyc = []; j = s
            while True:
                cyc.append(arr[j]); j = (j + k) % n
                if j == s: break
            m = median(cyc)
            ans += sum(abs(v - m) for v in cyc)
        return ans

a.t: Expected O(n) — linear-time selection per cycle (worst case degrades like quicksort).

w: Always median, never mean — with integer moves the median minimizes the sum of absolute deviations. Watch 64-bit accumulation (values up to 1e9, n up to 1e5 → sums near 1e14; in JS use regular numbers carefully or BigInt). Pitfalls: mishandling the circular wrap when collecting cycles, and assuming k divides n. Follow-up: minimize sum of squared deviations instead (then use the mean).
